name: fortinet-fortiedrv2
label: Fortinet FortiEDR v2
description: FortiEDR protects endpoints pre and post infection, stopping data breaches in real-time and automatically orchestrating incident investigation and response. This connector covers events, forensics, collectors, exceptions, IP sets, console incidents and scheduled ingestion keyed on event activity (lastSeen).

operations.title: Delete Collectors
operations.description: Deletes collector records from the Fortinet FortiEDR console inventory. Filter the deletion by device IDs, device names, or a last-seen cutoff; at least one filter is REQUIRED. The console's delete API requires the explicit deleteAll=true confirmation, which this operation always sends, and with no filter that confirmation deletes EVERY collector record in the organization, so an empty request is refused before it is ever sent. operations.title: Ingest Events
operations.description: Fetches every event whose Last Seen (or First Seen, per Time Field) falls in [From, To] and returns them already mapped to FortiSOAR alert payloads (external_id = eventId, severity clamped to the picklist). Built for the scheduled ingestion playbooks. FortiEDR links re-detections of the same process into the EXISTING event -- its firstSeen never moves -- so the default window is on Last Seen; a firstSeen window misses re-triggered events. The window is count-verified rather than paged: count-events is asked first, the fetch is one list-events request sized to that count (pageNumber is never sent; on FortiEDR 7.x it answers 200 with an empty page), and a short answer is re-read, then escalated by splitting the window, failing loudly rather than returning part of a window. Optional filters (Classifications, Severities, Device Name, Collector Groups, Organization) narrow the one query count-events and list-events share, so the count-verify holds on the filtered window.
